author: @abn

evidence.api_compatibility: No breaking change. The allowed_origins config syntax is extended to accept : and *.domain patterns; existing configurations behave identically. A new boolean field wildcard_port was added to the Origin struct, but it is internal and does not affect any public API, persistence format, or CLI contract.
evidence.documentation: docs/guide/configuration/README.md was updated to document wildcard port (:*) and wildcard domain (*.domain) syntax, and to add security warning sections for universal wildcards. Labels include documentation.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No human independently exercised the wildcard matching paths before merge. CI passed but CI does not test wildcard-origin acceptance from a real client. The to-do list requests concrete manual verification of the new behavior against the release candidate. No evidence of a regression risk; the wildcard feature is additive.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None. The single PR commit (e3db3d13) is the commit that was approved and merged as 6a5e307d. Zero post-approval churn.
evidence.review: @Geramy (security maintainer per contribute.md) performed a substantive review. He opened with a CHANGES_REQUESTED reviewing the implementation as a regex-vs-manual-string question, provided three inline comments requesting regex usage, then COMMENTED after the author incorporated regex for port parsing and domain matching. He APPROVED the final version on 2026-09-09T18:09:16Z. No other reviewers participated. The PR has the label rfc:required, and RFC #3427 was approved as referenced in the PR body.
evidence.security: @Geramy, a security-area maintainer, reviewed and approved. Subdomain matching uses strict dot-boundary enforcement (notexample.com, example.com.attacker.com, and badexample.com are all rejected against *.example.com). Universal wildcard (*) and (http://*:*) usage is documented with explicit security warnings in the config docs. No credential handling, code execution, or supply-chain changes are introduced.
evidence.tests: 106 unit tests in test_origin_utils.cpp covering positive/negative wildcard port parsing, subdomain dot-boundary enforcement, malformed input rejection, universal wildcard matching, default port normalization, and integration through is_origin_allowed() and is_websocket_origin_allowed(). CTest OriginUtilsTest suite ran 100% passing. 14/14 server_websocket_auth.py integration tests also passed. No tests weakened or deleted.

maintainer_todos.text: Start the Lemonade server with `LEMONADE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://192.168.1.50:*` and confirm that a browser or HTTP client connecting from `http://192.168.1.50:3000`, `:8080`, and `:5173` all succeed, while a connection from `http://192.168.1.51:3000` is rejected.

Start the server with `LEMONADE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://*.local:*` and confirm that connections from `http://dashboard.local:3000` and `http://dev.local:5173` are accepted, while `http://evil.local:3000` and `http://local:3000` are rejected.

subject: feat(server): support wildcard port and host matching in allowed origins (#3470)
summary: Adds wildcard port matching (:) and subdomain pattern matching (*.domain) to the allowed_origins configuration so local dev and homelab environments can connect without reconfiguring when frontend servers switch ports.
verdict_reason: The PR was reviewed by a security expert and merged cleanly with no post-approval churn, but the wildcard matching feature should be manually verified against the release candidate before shipping.
